name: angina-borderline
description: Borderline: hears the chest tightness and tells him to call 999, but gives no greeting or introduction, does not ask timing or whether the spray helped, and gives no reason or safety net.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Oh hello, is that the surgery? I'm ringing about my prescription.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's my prescription, for my angina spray. I've used a lot of it.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Oh. How are you feeling at the moment?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Well, I have a bit of a tight feeling in my chest. I am sitting down though.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Right. You need to ring 999 now.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: All right, I will. Thank you.

expect.flagsReason: 999 immediately matches the key and the red flag was acted on, though thinly.

greeting.reason: No name, no practice, caller never named, never asked who it was for.

information.reason: Asked how he was feeling, which unlocked the tightness; never asked when it started or whether the spray helped.

redFlag.reason: Spotted and acted on, but on partial information; 2 if the action is all that counts.

explanation.reason: Said 999 but gave no reason beyond "you need to" and no advice about getting worse.

manner.reason: Brusque with a worried, apologetic man; clear but not warm.
